evidence_boundary.frontier_scale_question: Can dependency-safe dephasing of checkpoint, collective, survivor-compute, and rejoin operations across 10,000-100,000 GPUs prevent failures from producing coherent megawatt-scale power shocks without burn loads, spare-compute redundancy, optimizer-state divergence, or loss of liveput?
modeled: facility bridge equations conditioned on local phase kernels
observed: attempted replayed discarded redistributed and canonical work

facility_bridge.facility_transform: separately calibrated electrical power-chain and cooling response models
facility_bridge.it_equation: P_IT(t) = sum_g P_GPU_g(t) + P_CPU(t) + P_NIC(t) + P_storage(t)
facility_bridge.plain_boundary: PW1 identifies local operation kernels. It does not observe rack, cooling, storage, network, or point-of-common-coupling power.

lc3_engine.line_ending_canonicalization: source identity accepts raw or CRLF-to-LF canonical bytes

canonical_work.completion_rule: both logical site quota identities committed for every canonical logical tick

estimands.checkpoint_related_interaction: sum of primary additive interaction over checkpoint_related_phases
estimands.primary_total_interaction: sum of primary additive interaction over all exclusive phases

execution_order.design: four-sequence Williams order, each sequence used twice

continue.during_active_failure: execute both logical site quotas sequentially on survivor and checkpoint by assigned cadence
continue.on_rejoin: copy canonical model and Adam state to rejoined site

restart.after_failure: replay deterministic logical quota identities until canonical frontier
restart.during_active_failure: perform no training and create no reduced-membership merge
restart.on_failure_start: restore both site states from latest checkpoint and roll logical tick back to checkpoint tick
